Before us this evening, we have a recommendation to resolve the preferred site for development of a new Northern Bellarine Aquatic Centre, encompassing of an outdoor 50-metre pool as well as further stages of development. In April 2019, the Morrison government announced an election commitment of $10 million in funding for the 50-metre outdoor pool in the North Bellarine. This was thanks to the tireless work of Senator Sarah Henderson in her role at the time as a member for Corangamite. The city, in turn, commissioned a scoping study to explore the costs and benefits of investing in a 50-metre outdoor pool in the Drysdale catchment area, a scoping study which reiterated what all Bellarine residents know, that such an investment is sorely needed. In March 2020, Council resolved to note the scoping study that identified two potential locations for the new pool, which stood up above the rest, those being the Drysdale Depot and the Drysdale Sporting Precinct. After extensive internal investigation and consulting the community advocacy group, the proposed location for the new 50-metre pool is the Drysdale Sporting Precinct. The key reasons for this proposal, when compared to the depot site, are accessibility to the North Bellarine community, this is by car, public transport or on foot, integration with local area, including local schools and other community facilities and the surrounding landscape, and as well as long-term financial and social sustainability, including the potential for the facility to become more fully integrated in the future. This centre will feature the 50-metre outdoor pool, a multi-purpose space, changing facilities and a pavilion. This will complete the first stage of an evolving vision, a vision to expand this centre to include aquatic therapy pools, learn-to-swim areas, the list goes on. This is to fill the gap that was identified in the independent scoping study, that the residents in the Northern Bellarine have lesser access to aquatic facilities than those in other parts of Greater Geelong. This has been a long time coming, and I thank Mayor Asher for his strong support on this issue, as I do my fellow Bellarine Councillor, Councillor Mason. I'm proud to be part of a council which is delivering $750,000 in this year's budget towards this project, to the $10 million committed by the federal government.
